name: Bard Emotionist
body:
The emotionist is a master of manipulating emotions through music.

Emotional Knack (Ex)

An emotionist adds half their class level (minimum 1) to Diplomacy checks to improve attitude or alleviate despair, Bluff checks to induce or alleviate despair or to hide your emotional state via deceive or lie, Intimidate checks to demoralize, induce despair, or exhort morale, and Sense Motive checks to discern emotional state via hunch or opposing a Bluff check.

Emotional Performance

An emotionist learns the following bardic performances.

Inspire Doubt (Su)

A 1st level emotionist can use their performance to inspire doubt in their enemies. To be affected, a target must be able to perceive the emotionist’s performance. An affected target must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the emotionist’s level + the emotionist’s Cha modifier) or be affected by the doubting condition for as long as the performance is maintained. This ability cannot raise the target’s condition above doubting. If the saving throws succeeds, the target is immune to the inspire doubt ability for 24 hours. Inspire doubt is a mind-affecting, emotion and despair effect. Inspire doubt can use audible or visual components. The emotionist must choose which component to use when starting his performance. This ability replaces fascinate.

Inspire Hope (Su)

A 1st level emotionist can use their performance to inspire hope in their allies (including themselves), bolstering them against despair and improving their combat abilities. To be affected, an ally must be able to perceive the emotionist’s performance.

An affected ally receives a +1 morale bonus on saving throws against fear and despair effects, attack rolls and weapon damage rolls. At 5th level, and every six emotionist levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +1, to a maximum of +4 at 17th level. Inspire hope is a mind-affecting, emotion and hope ability. Inspire hope can use audible or visual components. The emotionist must choose which component to use when starting his performance. This ability replaces inspire courage.

Inspire Rage (Su)

A 3rd level emotionist can use their performance to inspire fervor and rage in a target.

The target must be within 30 feet and able to see and hear the emotionist. If the target is unwilling they may make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the emotionist’s level + the emotionist’s Cha modifier). If they succeed, they may not be affected by inspire rage for 24 hours. An affected creature enters a rage gaining a +2 bonus on melee attack rolls, damage rolls and thrown weapon damage rolls, and Will saving throws. In addition, they take a -2 penalty on AC. The target also gains +2 temporary hit points per HD. These temporary hit points are lost first when the target takes damage, disappear when the performance ends, and are not replenished if the target enters a rage or is affected by inspire rage again within 1 minute of the ending of the performance. While under this effect, the target cannot use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skill (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride) or any ability that requires patience or concentration (such as spellcasting). At the end of the performance, the target is fatigued for a number of rounds equal to the rounds spent under the effect of the performance.

If the target falls unconscious, they are no longer affected by the performance.

At 11th and 20th levels the bonuses provided increase by 1 and the temporary hp per HD increase by 1.

Inspire rage is a mind-affecting, emotion and hope ability. Inspire rage can use audible or visual components.

This ability replaces inspire competence.

Emotional Master

At 5th level, an emotionist becomes a master at eliciting or alleviating emotions and can take 10 on any skill check detailed in the emotional knack ability above. In addition, once per day, the bard can take 20 on any such skill check as a standard action. He can use this ability one additional time per day for every six levels he possesses beyond 5th, to a maximum of three times per day at 17th level.

Incite Dread (Sp)

A 6th-level or higher emotionist can easily turn one’s doubts into fear as a standard action. They may target any enemy within 30 ft., that is able to see or hear the emotionist, and is currently subject to a despair effect by one of their performances.

The target must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the emotionist’s level + the emotionist’s Cha modifier) or be frightened for 1d6 rounds. If the creature succeeds at the saving throw or the frightened duration ends, they are shaken for as long as they are within 30 feet of the emotionist while they are maintaining the despaireffect-inducing performance. Incite dread does not disrupt the underlying performance. Incite dread is a mind-affecting, fear effect, and it relies on audible and visual components.

This ability replaces suggestion.

Heroic Encouragement (Sp)

A 9th-level or higher emotionist can spur their already hopeful allies into great heroics as a standard action. The affected ally must be within 30 feet, that is able to see or hear the emotionist, and is currently subject to a hope effect by one of their performances. The ally gains temporary hit points equal to 2d10 plus their Con modifier, and their morale bonuses from the hope effect are doubled. This effect lasts for 1d4 rounds. Heroic encouragement is a mind-affecting, emotion and hope effect, and it relies on audible and visual components. Heroic encouragement does not disrupt the underlying performance.

This ability replaces inspire greatness.

Dirge of Despair (Su)

An emotionist of 8th level or higher can use his performance to foster a sense of immense despair in his enemies, causing them to become despairing. To be affected, an enemy must be within 30 feet and able to see and hear the emotionist’s performance. The effect persists for as long as the enemy is within 30 feet and the emotionist continues the performance. The performance cannot cause a creature to become hopeless, even if the targets are already doubting from another effect. Dirge of despair is a mind-affecting, emotion and despair effect, and it relies on audible and visual components.

This ability replaces dirge of doom.

Calming Performance (Su)

An emotionist of 12th level or higher can use their performance to create an effect equivalent to the mass cure serious wounds, using the emotionist’s level as the caster level. In addition, this performance removes the doubting, despairing, and shaken condition from all those affected. Using this ability requires 4 rounds of continuous performance, and the targets must be able to see and hear the emotionist throughout the performance. Calming performance relies on audible and visual components.

This ability replaces soothing performance.

Hopeless Harmonic (Su)

An emotionist of 14th level or higher can use their performance to cause hopelessness in their enemies. To be affected, an enemy must be able to hear the emotionist perform and be within 30 feet. Each enemy within range receives a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the emotionist’s level + the emotionist’s Cha modifier) to negate the effect. If the save succeeds, the creature is immune to this ability for 24 hours. If the save fails, the target becomes hopeless for as long as the target can hear the bard’s performance. Hopeless harmonic relies on audible components.

This ability replaces frightening tune.

Hope Beyond Despair (Sp)

An emotionist of 15th level or higher can use their performance to help their allies push past any doubts or despair they might have. Any ally affected by heroic encouragement also has one despair or fear effect of the ally’s choice removed (with the exception of curses).

This ability replaces inspire heroics.

Mass Dread (Sp)

This ability functions just like incite dread, but allows an emotionist of 18th level or higher to incite dread into any number of creatures that they have already affected by a despair-effect-inducing performance. Incite dread is a mind-affecting, fear effect, and it relies on audible and visual components.

This ability replaces mass suggestion.
